raw_response:
This small piece of land near my home, only a little bigger than my compound, I use it for mixed crops — some vegetables and roots together, for eating at home. I am old now, sixty-four, so I do most of the work myself slowly, with help sometimes from a grandchild. I cannot afford to buy fertilizer from the shop this season, but I put the manure from my few chickens and the kitchen ashes on this plot because it is close to the house. The seeds I keep from last season, and on such a small garden plot I do not spray chemicals or pay for water — the rains of masika are coming and this plot is small enough to water by hand from the jerrycan when needed.
